newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT-Dlr may hurt if 112.20 yen floor crumbles.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT-Dlr may hurt if 112.20 yen floor crumbles.

text.p: A convincing break of key dollar support at 112.20 yen may signal a more serious pullback but it could also spur bottom-fishing, chartists said.

Chris Turner, a senior foreign exchange analyst at I.D.E.A. Inc, noted that 112.20 yen represents about a 61.8 percent Fibonnaci retracement of the rally from 110.55 on November 15 to 114.75 on December 2.
He contends a convincing break could signal the dollar is not just in a correction but in a more powerful down-move.
"I think it's pretty critical," he said.

The dollar briefly dipped below the 112.20 threshold earlier to 112.10 yen before bouncing higher. But Turner said, "It's got to break below (112.20) and stay below really on a daily basis (to) probably provide extra confirmation."
Should the dollar break convincingly below 112.20, it might target 111.55 yen near where a four-point trendline rising off of the April 1995 low (79.75) comes in, according to Turner.
"I think that'll be (a) crucial support level for the dollar because this trendline actually helped form the low at 110.50 (yen) in November," he said.

"You break below (111.55), then really this steep bull trend off the (79.75) low last April is ended," said Turner. "And that's when I think people will start to feel more confident that there is this large double-top in dollar/yen."
In late afternoon, the dollar once again drifted lower towards key support, trading around 112.30/35 yen at 1510 EST/2010 GMT, compared with 112.80/90 at the open.
Foreign Exchange Analytics Partner David Solin sketched support below 112.20 yen at around 111.80/70, which might trigger bottom-fishing.
"...usually what happens when you break a very good level like (112.20 yen) you get just a little spike lower and then it comes right back bid after some of those stops are triggered," Solin said.
